cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Name Your Backers
cards.instruction: Get someone to reveal who supports their position, who authorized it, and who benefits from it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I authorize the workshop closure notice, tell me who backed your decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The director approved it. Can I send it now?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not yet. You may add her name. Who else supported closing us?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sales. They're getting our floor space, but can we leave them out?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. Put Sales in the notice and invite them to the staff meeting. I want the name of whoever approved their new floor space before I approve one word.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 conditions notice authorization on naming backers; A3 grants name addition but not sending; A5 denies omission and requires the beneficiary approval name, so status controls each disclosure.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 director approval yields A3 added name and supporter question; B4 Sales benefit yields A5 public inclusion and transfer-authorizer demand.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants to send an authorized notice and B4 wants Sales excluded; A exact refusal exposes that selective disclosure.

heightening.evidence: B4 concealed benefit causes A5 to require attendance and approval attribution before the notice moves.

specificity.evidence: A1 workshop closure notice and B4 floor-space transfer establish concrete stakes and benefit; A3 closing us identifies A affected group.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 before I approve one word turns B repeated send request into stricter conditions; clear but more stern than witty.

coach2.inferred: Director approval of closure can coexist with A procedural control of the notice; A acts highest toward B.
coach2.missing: No essential fact missing; adding names in a draft does not mean the notice is already approved.
coach2.firstDefect: No comprehension defect found on rereading.
